source.title_on_document: Effects of AI-generated drawing on students' learning achievement and creativity in an ancient poetry course

paper_design_summary: Sixty second-year students in two intact Chinese-language classes at one high school in New Taipei City, Taiwan, studied two Pre-Qin poems over three weeks. One class (31 students) wrote vernacular descriptions of poem scenes and had Bing AI Copilot (OpenAI DALL-E) generate the pictures; the other class (29 students) drew the scenes by hand on a worksheet. The paper compares posttest achievement, self-reported creative tendency, motivation, self-efficacy, and cognitive load with independent-sample t-tests, and counts coded content elements (characters, environmental objects, emotions) in the two groups' drawings.

studies.label: Two-class comparison (GenAI drawing vs conventional drawing, ancient poetry course)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Learning mode, by intact class: one class used the GenAI drawing mode, the other the conventional drawing mode. The paper does not say how the two classes were chosen for each mode.
assignment.quote: These students were from two classes in the school's Chinese language curriculum. One class was the experimental group, while the other was the control group.

arms.name: Experimental group (GenAI drawing mode)
arms.description: Students read the poem, wrote a five- to ten-sentence vernacular description, and used Bing AI Copilot (DALL-E) to generate a matching picture; images were combined into a short video viewed on Google Cardboard

arms.name: Control group (conventional drawing mode)
arms.description: Students read the poem and drew scenes by hand on a worksheet with written descriptions

participants.exclusions: Whole-group Tables 3-6 and 9 use N = 31 and 29 (pp. 302-304). Table 7 uses experimental-group high/low creative-tendency subgroups of 17 and 14 (p. 303), and Table 8 uses control-group subgroups of 16 and 13 (p. 304); these are subgroups of the same study. For the drawing analysis only, three of the 60 students' drawings were excluded as irrelevant or incomplete (p. 305, Sections 4.7 and 4.7.1). Retained drawing counts and retained participant counts by arm are not stated, yet Table 10 still divides by 31 and 29.
participants.who: Second-grade high-school students, average age 16, from two classes of the school's Chinese language curriculum
participants.quote: The subjects of this study were 60 students in the second grade of a high school in New Taipei City, Taiwan. Their average age was 16 years old.

ai_tool.name_model: Bing AI - Copilot (Microsoft), based on OpenAI DALL-E image generation
ai_tool.how_used: After reading the poem, students wrote a five- to ten-sentence vernacular description and prompted the tool to generate a picture matching it (p. 300, Section 3.3, and p. 301, Figure 5); the generated images were combined into a short video and viewed in Google Cardboard (p. 301).

task.description: Depict the characters, scenes, and events of one of two ancient poems, Reed (jian jia) or Fisherman (yu fu): a GenAI-generated picture from the student's written description (experimental) or a hand drawing with description on a worksheet (control)
task.duration: One 100-minute session in week 2 of a 3-week procedure (Figure 3, p. 300)

outcomes.name: Content elements coded in students' drawings (Table 10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Drawings and their descriptions coded with the scheme in Tables 1 and 2 (characters, environmental objects, emotions and attitudes); Table 10 reports the total count per category by group with the per-student average in parentheses (N/31, N/29). Descriptive only, no test statistic. In the experimental group the scored picture is the AI-generated image from the student's prompt.

contrasts.reported: EG (% = N/31): Characters 57 (1.84), Environmental Objects 112 (3.61), Emotions and attitudes 24 (0.77); CG (% = N/29): Characters 52 (1.79), Environmental Objects 72 (2.48), Emotions and attitudes 22 (0.76). Counts only, no test reported.

outcomes.name: Creative tendency questionnaire (post)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Five-item 5-point Likert questionnaire adapted from Lai and Hwang (2014); Cronbach's alpha .79 (pre) and .77 (post) (p. 298). Pre-questionnaire means 3.85 (SD 0.55) EG vs 3.86 (SD 0.69) CG (p. 303). Prose and Table 4 disagree on the post means and p-value (see reported).
outcomes.delay: Week 3, after the Week 2 drawing activity; exact elapsed interval not stated (Figure 3, p. 300)

contrasts.reported: Table 4: Experimental group N = 31, Mean 3.72, SD 0.59; Control group N = 29, Mean 3.89, SD 0.61; t = -1.07, d = 0.28, p = .29. The text (Section 4.2) instead gives post means 3.73 (SD = 0.59) and 3.88 (SD = 0.61), t = -1.07, p = .64.

outcomes.name: Learning achievement posttest
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: 100-point posttest developed by two experienced Chinese-language instructors: 20 multiple-choice items (60 points), eight multiple-answer items (32 points), one open-ended item (8 points) (p. 298, Section 3.2). Scoring personnel and an expert-rating procedure are not specified. Not a creativity outcome; recorded because it is the paper's main result. Prose SD (9.06) differs from Table 3 SD (9.60) for the experimental group.
outcomes.delay: Week 3, after the Week 2 drawing activity; exact elapsed interval not stated (Figure 3, p. 300)

contrasts.reported: Table 3: Experimental group N = 31, Mean 71.77, SD 9.60; Control group N = 29, Mean 66.07, SD 8.31; t = 2.45*, d = 0.64 (*p < .05). Text (Section 4.1): experimental SD 9.06, t = 2.45, p = .02.

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1: the two conditions are two intact classes (p. 297, Section 3.1: 'One class was the experimental group, while the other was the control group'); people were not randomly assigned, and the paper does not say how each class was matched to a mode. Criterion 2: 60 students analyzed (31 + 29). Criterion 3: the only measure scored on the output is a descriptive count of coded content elements in the drawings (Table 10, p. 305), closest to elaboration, with no test; creativity itself is a self-reported creative-tendency questionnaire (Table 4), which does not qualify. The only randomization in the paper is the choice of six interviewees per group (p. 300).

one_line_finding: Two intact high-school classes (31 students with Bing AI Copilot/DALL-E drawing vs 29 with hand drawing): posttest 71.77 (SD 9.60) vs 66.07 (SD 8.31), t = 2.45, d = 0.64, p = .02 (p. 302, Section 4.1 and Table 3); self-reported creative tendency 3.72 vs 3.89, t = -1.07, d = 0.28, p = .29 (p. 303, Table 4); the GenAI group's drawings carried more coded content elements, for example environmental objects 112 (3.61 per student) vs 72 (2.48), with no test (p. 305, Table 10).
